Using unfired brass, use a tapered expander to neck up to .35, anneal, then neck back down adjusting the sizing die to start the shoulder lower and lower in small increments, checking it in your rifle after every adjustment. Start the process with the die adjusted long enough that the bolt won't close on a sized case, and keep adjusting shorter until the bolt closes with slight resistance, then load and fire form that case and you're done. In this way, you end up with cases without the initial stretch ring, and with periodic annealing they should last quite a few reloadings.
